candidate.publisher: Louisiana Secretary of State, Commercial Division
candidate.availability: paid request-defined multi-entity search; electronic ordering is account and payment mediated, with no anonymous recurring statewide extract or documented delivery format
candidate.price: $25 for the first 40 entity records plus $0.01 per additional record

observed_evidence: The Commercial Division offers paid custom multi-entity computer queries but publishes no complete active-statewide product, anonymous route, recurring cadence, delivery format, schema, sample, aggregate size, or checksum.
The separate account and token-gated Commercial API is rate-limited to 18 calls per minute and 1,000 search results, has no pagination or changed-since route, and is not a statewide bulk substitute.
Charter Number is only a candidate stable key because uniqueness wording does not establish length, non-reuse, or continuity through conversion, merger, reinstatement, termination, and migration.
Charter, substatus, and annual-report standing are legal filing conditions rather than proof of current operation, while registered offices expressly need not be places of business.
Public-record inspection and a customer-application API do not establish indefinite retention, transformation, geocoding, derived-publication, or redistribution rights.
required_exclusions: registered agents, registered offices and service-of-process addresses
officers, directors, members, managers, owners, individual trade-name applicants and every natural-person role and address
name-reservation contacts, email, phone, signature and direct-contact fields
tax, payment, account credential, financial and non-registry government identifiers; preserve only a contract-confirmed public charter key
filing images, documents and narrative or free-text fields
states.strongest_bounded_next_action: Ask the Louisiana Commercial Division for a written quote and unsigned terms for one complete as-of legal-entity extract, with exact person-free schema, aggregate size, type/status/address dictionaries, Charter Number lifecycle, recurring full/delta/deletion/replay/checksum contract, secure unattended delivery, platform-change notice, and explicit retention, transformation, geocoding, derived-publication and redistribution rights. Do not create an account, accept terms, buy a token, order rows, enumerate the API or portal, or implement a connector first.

candidate.publisher: Minnesota Secretary of State, Business Services
candidate.availability: account-gated ZIP and CSV containing active registered names and primary addresses; available once or weekly through MBLS Transaction History

observed_evidence: The 2025 Active Business Data guide publishes a 16-column layout and illustrative output with separate ZIP and ZIP extension, but no current count, bytes, manifest, checksum, or control total.
The candidate covers records classified active across multiple entity and assumed-name types, with a Housing Cooperative discrepancy between the current landing page and dated guide.
File Number plus Business Filing Type is documented as unique within this product but lacks non-reuse and lifecycle guarantees; the stronger static Master ID belongs only to another product.

Active is a recognition and renewal condition rather than operating proof, and the primary business address type lacks a complete value domain proving organization control rather than agent, party, or home use.

Weekly account delivery exists, but full-replacement, disappearance, deletion, correction, replay, checksum, unattended access, controlling-license, retention, geocoding, and derived-publication semantics remain unresolved.
required_exclusions: registered agents, registered offices, service addresses, home addresses and every address not proven organization-controlled
assumed-name natural-person holders, business parties, officers, managers, organizers, incorporators and every natural-person name and address
email, phone, signature and direct-contact fields
tax, payment, account, financial and non-registry government identifiers; preserve only contract-confirmed public registry keys
filing images, documents and narrative or free-text fields
states.strongest_bounded_next_action: Ask Minnesota SOS which license controls Active Business Data and request written permission for retention, organization-only transformation, geocoding and derived publication; a current header-only person-free sample and aggregate size; exact address-type values and File Number lifecycle; weekly replacement/deletion/replay/checksum semantics; and an approved unattended delivery method. Do not create an MBLS account, accept terms, pay, acquire a fixture, automate Transaction History, or implement a connector first.

candidate.publisher: Alabama Secretary of State, Business Services Division
candidate.product: Business Entity Database / Government Records Inquiry System
candidate.availability: free per-entity inquiry only; no published bulk file, API, feed, recurring export, or supported automation route
candidate.price: No bulk business-entity price is published; ad hoc public-record copies are $1 per page plus quoted outside costs

observed_evidence: The current SOS entity database exposes individual searches only; its downloads page contains filing forms rather than an entity dataset, and no recurring bulk business-entity product is priced.
A 2021 internal records authority describes the database and a few fields but is not a current export schema, sample, row count, byte size, checksum, manifest, or status codebook.
Entity ID changed from six to nine displayed digits by adding leading zeroes and is continued through at least some conversions, but universal non-reuse and lifecycle behavior remain undocumented.
Exists is legal-record status rather than operating proof, and elimination of SOS annual reports effective October 2024 increases address and status staleness risk.

The official $1,500 full and $300 weekly bulk prices apply to UCC data, not business entities; public inspection supplies no affirmative transformation, geocoding, publication, or redistribution license.

candidate.publisher: Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions, Division of Corporate and Consumer Services
candidate.availability: paid complete text file delivered through a DFI-created ShareFile subscriber account; one-time, weekly Tuesday, or monthly second-Tuesday schedules require mailed Form 51 and prepayment
candidate.price: $40 per full database file; the separate additions-only monthly new-formations file is $5

observed_evidence: DFI sells the complete corporate database as a text file for $40 per snapshot through ShareFile, with one-time, weekly Tuesday, and monthly second-Tuesday order options.

The data-services page names only legal name, registered agent and office address, entity type, formation date, current status, and annual-report indicator; it publishes no exact layout, sample, delimiter, encoding, count, bytes, checksum, or manifest.

The seven-character DFI Entity ID is assigned when first organized and public status/type dictionaries exist, but bulk inclusion, non-reuse, conversion, merger, reinstatement, and migration continuity are not guaranteed.
DFI expressly says it is not a registry of all businesses and cannot certify legal operation; the July 2026 active count of 635,017 also excludes miscellaneous entities and foreign registered names.

The only bulk-listed address is registered agent or office data, which is ineligible for entity geocoding; full-snapshot deletion, correction, replay, unattended ShareFile, retention, transformation, geocoding, and redistribution terms are unpublished.
